title: Hired On The Last Day Of The Month
description:
Report the `name` of every employee hired on the last calendar day of their hire month (the 28th, 29th, 30th or 31st, whichever is correct for that specific month).

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT name FROM employees
WHERE hire_date = date(hire_date, 'start of month', '+1 month', '-1 day');
hint: Don't hardcode `'-31'` or check against a fixed day number — months have different lengths (and February has 28 or 29). Compute "the day before the start of next month" instead, and SQLite's date() modifiers handle the varying month lengths for you.
outputExplanation: None of the 8 hire dates fall on the last day of their month, so the result is empty. Hidden tests demonstrate June 30 and February 29 (leap year) as qualifying last-day hires.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
No one hired on the last day of any month
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'E','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','E',100000,1,NULL,'2022-01-15'),(2,'B','E',90000,1,1,'2022-02-14');

tests.name: One employee hired on a month's last day
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'E','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','E',100000,1,NULL,'2022-01-31'),(2,'B','E',90000,1,1,'2022-02-14');

tests.name: Multiple employees on last days of different months
February 28 in non-leap year — is last day
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'E','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','E',100000,1,NULL,'2022-02-28');

tests.name: February 29 in leap year — is last day
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'E','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-02-29');
